- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.75) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.25) or shows strong negative spikes, model over-forecasts; reduce forecast to avoid bearish overcorrection.  
- Model often under-responds to sharp price spikes in history — if last 3–5 prices show a steep rise, forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–2% to capture momentum.  
- Model exhibits lag in mean reversion — if history shows a clear trend (e.g., 5–7 days of rising prices), forecast should not immediately revert to mean; allow 1–2 days of gradual correction.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model frequently overestimates near-term (first 5–7 days) and underestimates long-term (last 10–15 days) — adjust downward in early days and upward in late days if sentiment is bullish.  
- If sentiment history shows a recent reversal (e.g., from 0.5 to 0.25), model often fails to adjust — apply a “reversal buffer” to forecast 1–2 days of consolidation before resuming trend.
